Definition: from G1537 and G4126; to depart by ship:--sail (away, thence).
BiblicalUsage: ekpléō turns up where the Bible says to sail away. In Acts 15:39, the text says "that they departed asunder one from the other." In Acts 18:18, the text says "and sailed thence into Syria."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ekpléō shows us that the gospel was never meant to stay where it started — it goes out, because God sends it out. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Jerusalem Council; Paul and Barnabas Part Ways
